title: Mexico’s Exports Grew 37.9 Percent and Imports 33.1 Percent Annually in September
author: Clara Zepeda
content:
_This article by Clara Zepeda originally appeared in the[October 27, 2026
edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/27/economia/las-
exportaciones-crecieron-379-por-ciento-y-las-importaciones-331-por-ciento-
anual-en-septiembre), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

In September 2026, merchandise exports increased 37.9 percent annually, driven
by non-automotive manufactures, which rebounded 53 percent compared to the
ninth month of the year, figures from the National Institute of Statistics and
Geography (Inegi) revealed.

According to timely foreign trade information (merchandise trade balance), the
most significant increases within manufactured products were in exports of
electrical and electronic equipment and devices, with growth of 94.7 percent,
amid the technology boom in the United States and the world; they were
followed by mining and metallurgy products, 15.5 percent, and special
machinery and equipment for various industries, 14.7 percent.

Thus, **84.40 percent of Mexican goods were exported to the United States**
through September 2026; to the rest of the world, 15.20 percent.

According to Inegi, the value of merchandise exports was **77,797 million
dollars** last September, an unprecedented figure for a September, and an
amount 37.9 percent higher than the ninth month of last year, its best advance
for a ninth month of the year.

This was due to growth of 38.8 percent in non-oil exports and 9.6 percent in
oil exports. Within non-oil exports, there were annual increases of 43.5
percent in those destined for the United States and 16.4 percent in those
channeled to the rest of the world.

For its part, the value of merchandise imports was 78,403 million dollars,
also a figure never seen before for a ninth month of the year, and represented
an annual increase of 33.1 percent.

Intermediate-use goods were imported for a value of 63,103 million dollars, a
level 38.8 percent higher than that reported in September 2025. In turn, this
figure derived from advances of 39.6 percent in imports of non-oil
intermediate-use products and 26 percent in those of oil intermediate-use
goods.

For their part, imports of capital goods reached 5,477 million, which implied
an annual rise of 18.7 percent.

Thus, in September 2026, imports exceeded exports by 606.1 million dollars,
according to timely trade balance data.

### In Nine Months

From January to September 2026, the value of total exports added up to 627,194
million dollars, 30.4 percent more than during the first nine months of 2025.

Sales abroad were driven by an increase of 31.4 percent in non-oil exports, as
a decline of 0.2 percent was reported in oil exports.

In the first nine months of this year, the structure of the value of
merchandise exports was manufactured goods, 92.3 percent; non-oil extractive
products, 2.6 percent; oil goods, 2.6 percent; and agricultural and livestock
products, 2.5 percent.

The accumulated value of total imports, for its part, was 617,940 million
dollars, which represented an increase of 27.5 percent compared to that
observed in the same period of 2025. Within it, non-oil imports rose 28.2
percent and oil imports, 19.4 percent annually.

The structure of the value of imports was made up of intermediate-use goods,
80.4 percent; consumer goods, 12.5 percent; and capital goods, 7.1 percent.

For the first nine months of 2026, the trade balance showed a **surplus of
9,254 million dollars**. In the same period of 2025, it registered a deficit
of 3,398 million dollars.
